newsitem.title: FRANCE: IGC clears Eurotunnel freight service after tests.
newsitem.headline: IGC clears Eurotunnel freight service after tests.

text.p: The Intergovernmental Commission responsible for Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel has authorised the resumption of the Shuttle freight service halted since a fire broke out in the tunnel last year, officials from both bodies said on Thursday.
They said the authorisation hinged on a series of safety tests to be completed by June 15.

"Taking into account the commitments to carry out the recommendations resulting from the investigation into the November 18, 1996 fire and the security committee's opinion, the Intergovernmental Commission has accepted Eurotunnel's proposals relative to the resumption of Shuttle freight services on the condition that tests be conducted between now and June 15," the IGC said in a statement issued after a meeting in Paris.
A spokeswoman for Eurotunnel said the company planned to resume full Shuttle freight service on June 15 after carrying out two series of tests, the second with non-paying passengers.
The Commission last week withheld authorisation for the resumption of the service after the British delegation expressed safety concerns, notably about the design of the freight wagons.
Eurotunnel had sought to resume freight traffic on May 15 and increase it gradually to full service by June 15.

The resumption of freight traffic in addition to its other services is crucial for the company, which is trying to persuade its shareholders and bankers to back its 9 billion pound ($14.8 billion) debt restructuring survival plan.

Sources close to the investigation say a French judicial inquiry is expected to blame arson for the blaze, which started in a freight wagon at the Calais end of the subsea tunnel and caused several injuries and 200 million pounds of damage. ($ = 0.607 British Pounds)
